task: STEP 0 -- Alpha Memory / Feedback Loop Existing-Code Audit (read-only)
head: 9f228723fad5406c72e62beca67ec70ea0fdb004
note: Local worktree (including uncommitted changes) was inspected directly with grep/read against files on disk -- not git history, not GitHub, not HEAD alone.
overall_verdict_explanation: The Development Plan's own 'MVP Lite memory' half (static Alpha taxonomy + static entity-exposure seed) is genuinely ALREADY_IMPLEMENTED_ACTIVE -- it is real, in the live runtime path, and exactly matches what the Plan describes as MVP scope. The Phase-2 'adaptive memory' half (persistent structure identity / phi-ID, cross-run causal-chain matching, invalidation-event persistence, reason-code lifecycle, memory-based activation modulation, human-review feedback into future runs) is essentially NOT_IMPLEMENTED anywhere in the codebase -- not disconnected, not half-built, simply never started, with exactly ONE incidental, unintentional reusable primitive found (a deterministic factor+ticker node-id scheme in the Structure Extractor, built for graph deduplication, never used for cross-run identity). Calling the whole system PARTIAL_FOUNDATION_ONLY would understate that MVP Lite genuinely works today; calling it NOT_IMPLEMENTED would be wrong for the same reason. MIXED is the only verdict that is true of both halves at once.

M1_static_alpha_taxonomy_memory.evidence: comqutor_alpha/alpha_library/alpha_taxonomy_v1.yaml + alpha_loader.py -- versioned, hash-guarded, loaded on every run.

M2_static_entity_exposure_seed.evidence: comqutor_alpha/config/entity_alpha_exposure_seed_v0.1.yaml + exposure/seed_loader.py -- versioned, hash-guarded, loaded on every run.

M3_exposure_history_persistence.evidence: entity_alpha_exposures DB table (storage/db/schema.py) + entity_alpha_exposures.json artifact -- a full per-run snapshot is genuinely written every run.

M4_exposure_history_reused_across_runs.evidence: No function anywhere queries a DIFFERENT run's entity_alpha_exposures row. repository.get_entity_alpha_exposures(run_id) and get_entity_alpha_exposures() (routes_research.py) are always scoped to the ONE current run_id being displayed. Only the STATIC seed value (same number every run) is reused -- never an outcome from a prior run.

M5_persistent_structure_identity.evidence: No deliberate cross-run structure-identity feature exists. An INCIDENTAL, reusable primitive exists (structure_extractor.py::_make_node -- id=_slug(_display_label(canonical_factor, ticker)), deterministic and stable across runs of the same ticker) but it is never compared/matched across runs by any code -- see reusable_foundations.

M6_stable_phi_id.evidence: No 'phi'/'phi_id'/'phi_token' symbol, field, column, or config key exists anywhere in code, schema, or config. The word appears only in docs/specs/development_plan_v1.0_reference_index.md (a false-positive grep hit, unrelated) and the Development Plan docx itself (as a deferred patent concept).

M7_cross_run_causal_chain_matching.evidence: No code loads two different runs' structure graphs/activations and matches recurring chains. comqutor_alpha/evaluation/cross_run.py is an offline QA harness that aggregates metrics across GOLDEN TEST CASES (fixture-based regression evaluation), not across real research runs' Alpha outcomes -- unrelated concept sharing only the name.

M8_invalidation_event_detection.evidence: invalidation_registry.py's conditions are static Product-authored text, looked up by alpha_id and displayed verbatim in the Conflict Radar Evidence UI (conflict_evidence_ui.py). No code ever evaluates a condition against actual evidence/claim text to detect whether it has been triggered.

M9_invalidation_event_persistence.evidence: No event type for 'an invalidation condition fired' exists anywhere -- nothing to persist because nothing is ever detected (see M8).

M10_non_execution_event_persistence.evidence: The codebase has no trading-execution/portfolio-action concept at all (the Development Plan's own MVP scope guard: 'must never emit bare Buy/Sell/Hold instructions... automated trading... explicitly out of MVP scope'), so a 'non-execution event' is not even a defined concept yet, let alone persisted.

M11_reason_code_lifecycle.evidence: blocked_reason_codes/cap_reason_codes/admissibility reason_codes are all computed FRESH every run from that run's own current inputs (activation_scorer_v2.py, conflict_admissibility.py -- both have zero repository/DB imports). No code tracks a reason code being raised, persisted, and later cleared/resolved over time.

M12_historical_memory_lookup.evidence: No function of the shape 'get_alpha_history(ticker, alpha_id)' or 'get_prior_run(ticker)' exists anywhere in comqutor_alpha/.

M13_memory_based_activation_modulation.evidence: activation_scorer_v2.py and exposure_engine.py import no repository/DB module at all -- architecturally incapable of reading any historical state, confirmed by direct inspection of every import statement in both files.

M14_human_review_feedback_into_future_ru.evidence: grep across comqutor_alpha/ for evidence_review_summary_v2/item2_blind_holdout5 returns zero production-code hits -- only test files reference these artifacts. Review data exists; it changes nothing at runtime.

M15_feedback_loop_artifact_api_visibilit.evidence: run_audit.json (the most comprehensive existing audit artifact) has no memory/feedback-loop section of any kind.

M16_feedback_loop_ui_visibility.evidence: No frontend component (grepped all of frontend/src/components, frontend/src/pages) renders anything related to memory, feedback loops, or cross-run history. The one 'history' hit found (ProcessingPage.test.tsx) is unrelated ETA-estimation history for a progress spinner.

q1_stable_cross_run_structure_identity.how_generated: Deterministic string slug of (canonical_factor, ticker) via _display_label()/_slug() -- pure functions, no run_id, no timestamp, no randomness involved.
q1_stable_cross_run_structure_identity.survives_across_runs: YES, by construction -- the same (factor, ticker) pair always produces the identical id string in every run's structure_graph.json, forever, with no code change needed.
q1_stable_cross_run_structure_identity.actually_used_cross_run: NO -- confirmed no code anywhere loads two different runs' structure_graph.json and compares/matches node ids across them. It exists purely as an intra-run deduplication key today.
q1_stable_cross_run_structure_identity.important_caveat: Only the special-cased factor 'Revenue Growth' is ticker-scoped in its id (e.g., 'nvda_revenue_growth'); every OTHER canonical factor's id is ticker-INDEPENDENT (e.g., 'ai_demand' would be the same id for NVDA, AMD, or any ticker). A future per-ticker phi-ID design would need to decide whether to change this scoping -- itself a PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED, not something to infer.

q2_phi_id_equivalent.docs_only: YES -- the Development Plan docx's patent-mapping table names phi-tokens as a deferred Phase 2 concept.

q3_invalidation_conditions.where_evaluated: NOWHERE -- invalidation_registry.load_invalidation_registry()'s only consumers are conflict_evidence_ui.py (display) and week4_persistence.py (storage passthrough of the already-static text for API/UI). No code path checks whether a condition's text describes something that has actually happened.
q3_invalidation_conditions.what_happens_when_triggered: N/A -- nothing can trigger it; there is no detection mechanism.
q3_invalidation_conditions.event_persisted: N/A -- no event exists to persist.

q4_failed_expired_invalidated_suppressed.stored: PARTIALLY, for one specific meaning of 'suppressed' only
q4_failed_expired_invalidated_suppressed.detail: conflict_detector.py's own arbitration.candidate_evaluations DOES persist a per-pair 'suppressed'/'rejected'/'admitted' outcome with reason_codes, per run -- but this is a WITHIN-RUN structural/evidentiary outcome (did this candidate conflict pair clear the evidence/B2 gate this run), not a cross-run 'this Alpha's thesis failed/expired over time' concept. No future run ever reads a prior run's candidate_evaluations back in (see M4/M12).
q4_failed_expired_invalidated_suppressed.reason_codes: Yes, exist and are descriptive (REASON_NO_LOCAL_STRUCTURE_SUPPORT etc.) but computed fresh every run, never accumulated.
q4_failed_expired_invalidated_suppressed.lifecycle: None -- no code tracks a reason code's state changing over time.

q5_any_historical_state_modifies_b4_acti.trace: activation_scorer_v2.py and exposure_engine.py -- the two modules that jointly determine B4's activation_score and cap_reason_codes -- both have ZERO import of comqutor_alpha.storage.db.repository or any other persistence module (confirmed by reading every import statement in both files). They are pure, stateless functions of the CURRENT run's own alpha_matches/graph/exposure-seed inputs. It is therefore architecturally impossible today for a prior run's score, a prior conflict outcome, retained graph state, or human-review data to affect B4.

q6_entity_exposure_history.B_historical_exposure_is_persisted: YES, per-run only (entity_alpha_exposures table/artifact) -- but this is a snapshot of THIS run's computed exposure, not an accumulated cross-run history record.
q6_entity_exposure_history.C_historical_exposure_is_read_on_later_r: NO for per-run records (see M4). YES, trivially, for the STATIC seed's historical_mapping number, which is the same fixed value every run regardless of what actually happened in any prior run.
q6_entity_exposure_history.D_historical_exposure_changes_activation: YES, via the static seed's historical_mapping (50% weight of the exposure formula, exposure_engine.py) feeding into B4's exposure-based blocking (REASON_LOW_ENTITY_EXPOSURE).
q6_entity_exposure_history.E_current_implementation_is: STATIC. The word 'historical' in historical_mapping refers to a human-authored prior belief baked into a YAML seed file at seed-approval time, never to anything the system itself measured or learned from actual past runs.

q7_write_only_foundation.component: structure_graphs DB table + structure_graph.json (including the stable factor+ticker node id)
q7_write_only_foundation.writes: per-run graph, with a node-id scheme that happens to be cross-run-stable

q8_shadow_read_path.detail: No component was found that reads historical/persisted data but keeps it isolated from official results (the strict definition of SHADOW_READ_PATH). The closest adjacent concept, Entity Exposure's shadow/draft_shadow MODE (B3), is a real, already-classified, unrelated concept: it reads the CURRENT run's own just-computed exposure and deliberately withholds it from affecting THIS SAME run's activation -- it never reads a prior run's history at all, so it does not qualify as a history-reading shadow path.

q9_dead_or_disconnected_alpha_memory_com.detail: No file/symbol was found that appears purpose-built for Alpha Memory and is now orphaned/disconnected. Everything discovered either (a) is fully active for its OWN, non-memory purpose (fingerprinting, request dedup, within-run claim integrity, QA golden-case harness), or (b) was never built at all. The one reusable primitive (structure node ids) is not 'disconnected from Alpha Memory' -- it was never connected to it in the first place; it exists for graph deduplication.

q10_unused_db_columns_tables_migrations.detail: Inspected every table in comqutor_alpha/storage/db/schema.py (schema_migrations, alpha_matches, structure_graphs, alpha_activations, entity_alpha_exposures, alpha_conflicts, research_runs, agent_outputs, research_run_progress). No column or table name (phi_id, structure_signature, invalidated_at, supersedes_run_id, memory_*, feedback_*) suggests planned-but-unbuilt Alpha Memory schema. research_runs.request_fingerprint exists but serves request-dedup, not structure identity (see q1 caveat and NOT_MEMORY_RELATED components).

q11_tests_specifying_intended_feedback_b.detail: Grepped tests/ for alpha_memory, feedback_loop, phi_id, structure_identity, memory_modul* -- zero hits. No test or fixture anywhere encodes an intended-but-unbuilt Alpha Memory contract.

q12_evidence_review_feeds_future_runs.evidence: grep -rl 'evidence_review_summary_v2|item2_blind_holdout5' comqutor_alpha/ returns zero files. Every reference is in tests/ or docs/audit_artifacts/. No production code path reads these artifacts.

q13_graph_persistence_sufficiency_for_st.answer: YES, already sufficient for a v1 phi-ID without touching the Structure Extractor's extraction logic itself
q13_graph_persistence_sufficiency_for_st.detail: structure_extractor.py already computes and persists a deterministic, cross-run-stable node id (factor+ticker slug) for every node in every run's structure_graph.json. A cross-run matcher could be built entirely as a NEW, separate read-side component that loads N runs' structure_graph.json files and groups nodes by this existing id -- no change to _make_node()/_extract_factors()/the extraction pipeline would be required. The only design question (ticker-scoping consistency across all factors, not just 'Revenue Growth') is a PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED, not an extraction-logic gap.

q14_retention_logic.detail: No retention/deletion policy exists anywhere in comqutor_alpha/ (zero grep hits for 'retention'). Every run's artifacts (DB rows and JSON files under outputs/runs/) persist indefinitely by default. This is FAVORABLE for a future Alpha Memory feature: the raw materials a cross-run matcher or invalidation-event store would need are not being destroyed today -- they simply are not being read back.

q15_components_to_reuse_vs_duplicate: structure_extractor.py's factor+ticker node-id scheme -- reuse as the seed of a v1 stable structure identity; do not invent a parallel id scheme.

comqutor_alpha.regression.authority_contract's APPROVED_GOLD/DOCUMENTED_EXPECTATION/PROVISIONAL_AI_PREDICTED/REJECTED_OR_SUPERSEDED vocabulary -- an existing, precise pattern for 'how confident is this classification, and can it affect production acceptance' that maps well onto any future invalidation-event confidence/authority question, if Product ever defines one.

comqutor_alpha.storage.db.repository's existing per-run read/write patterns (get_entity_alpha_exposures, get_research_run_record, etc.) -- extend with a new, explicitly cross-run query rather than building a second persistence layer.

run_audit.json's existing additive-section convention (activation_summary, conflict_summary, entity_exposure, ...) -- the natural place to add a future 'memory_summary' section, never a new top-level artifact file duplicating this one.

M14 human-review feedback into future runs
product_decisions_required: Whether a future stable structure identity should be ticker-scoped for EVERY canonical factor (today only 'Revenue Growth' is) -- changing this changes what 'the same structure' means across tickers.
Phi-similarity thresholds (how similar must two runs' evidence be to count as 'the same recurring causal chain') -- no existing authority defines this; must not be invented.

Memory weights (how much a historical signal should influence a new run's activation score, if at all) -- no existing authority defines this; activation_scorer_v2.py's frozen formula must not be silently extended.
Decay/expiry formulas for how long a persisted invalidation/non-execution event should remain influential -- no existing authority defines this.

Reason-code semantics for a NEW cross-run event type (e.g., what does 'this Alpha's thesis expired' mean precisely, and what reason code names it) -- no existing authority defines this; the existing 4 canonical B4 reason codes are for a different (within-run qualification) purpose and must not be silently repurposed.

Whether/how Evidence Review's human-adjudicated labels should ever be allowed to influence a future run (today they are explicitly audit-only) -- a genuine product-scope question, not an engineering one.

Which of the two readings of John's original 'feedback loop' complaint is meant (see docs/audit_artifacts/section_f_feedback_loop_spec_search_v0.1.3.json) -- this audit does not resolve that ambiguity, it only maps what exists today.
